name: Azure Machine Learning
oneLiner: End-to-end platform to train, deploy and manage machine-learning models.
whatItIs: Azure Machine Learning is Azure's managed platform for the full ML lifecycle: prepare data, train and tune models on managed compute, track experiments, register models, and deploy them to real-time or batch endpoints — with MLOps built in. It supports any framework (PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit) plus automated ML and a designer for low-code building, and integrates with ADLS, Synapse and Azure DevOps/GitHub for CI/CD. It's the workspace Azure data-science teams use to take a model from experiment to governed production; for foundation-model/generative AI, Azure pairs it with Azure OpenAI Service.

inPractice.narrative: A team reads training data from ADLS into an Azure ML workspace, runs an AutoML or custom training job on a managed compute cluster that scales up for the job and back down after, and tracks metrics across runs. The winning model is registered, versioned, and deployed to a managed online endpoint the app calls. An Azure ML pipeline (wired into GitHub Actions) retrains and redeploys as data changes. Compute is consumed only during jobs and while endpoints are live.

coreConcepts.detail: The top-level container tying together compute, data assets, models, experiments and endpoints — the hub everything in Azure ML lives under.
Managed compute instances (dev) and compute clusters (training) that autoscale and can scale to zero between jobs, so you pay for job time not idle nodes.
AutoML tries algorithms/hyperparameters for you on tabular/vision/NLP tasks; the Designer offers drag-and-drop low-code pipelines — alongside full code-first SDK/CLI.
Training runs are tracked jobs with logged metrics, parameters and artifacts, making experiments reproducible and comparable.
Register/version models, then deploy to managed online endpoints (real-time, autoscaled) or batch endpoints for bulk scoring.
Pipelines plus Azure DevOps/GitHub Actions enable CI/CD for models — automated train, evaluate, deploy with governance.

whenToUse: End-to-end ML on Azure: train, tune, deploy, monitor with governance.
Managed training on autoscaling (scale-to-zero) compute clusters.
Low-code (AutoML/Designer) or full code-first model development.
Productionising models with pipelines, registry and CI/CD (MLOps).
Teams integrated with ADLS, Synapse and Azure DevOps/GitHub.
whenNotToUse: Simple in-warehouse predictions — Synapse/SQL ML options may be enough.
Just consuming a foundation model — use Azure OpenAI Service directly.
Tiny one-off experiments where a local notebook suffices.
Purely analytical workloads with no ML component.

keyFacts.label: Scope
keyFacts.value: Full ML lifecycle: prep, train, tune, deploy, monitor.

source.quote: Azure Machine Learning is a cloud service that accelerates and manages the machine learning (ML) project lifecycle. ML professionals, data scientists, and engineers use it in their daily workflows to train and deploy models and manage machine learning operations (MLOps).

keyFacts.label: Compute
keyFacts.value: Managed instances + autoscaling clusters (scale to zero).

keyFacts.label: Build modes
keyFacts.value: Code-first SDK/CLI, AutoML, and low-code Designer.

source.quote: Azure Machine Learning designer: Use the designer to train and deploy ML models without writing any code. Drag and drop datasets and components to create ML pipelines. … Automated machine learning UI … Python SDK (v2) … Azure CLI (v2).
The Azure Machine Learning managed endpoints abstract the required infrastructure for both batch or real-time (online) model scoring (inferencing).

keyFacts.label: MLOps
keyFacts.value: Pipelines + Azure DevOps/GitHub CI/CD, model registry.

source.quote: Some key features enabling MLOps include: Git integration, MLflow integration, Machine learning pipeline scheduling, Azure Event Grid integration for custom triggers, Ease of use with CI/CD tools like GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps.

keyFacts.label: Billing
keyFacts.value: Underlying VM compute per job/endpoint + storage (no platform surcharge).

pricingShape: Azure ML has no separate platform fee — you pay for the underlying Azure compute and storage. Training clusters bill for VM time while running and can scale to zero between jobs, so training cost is essentially job-time; dev compute instances bill until stopped. Managed online endpoints run continuously and bill for their VMs even when idle — the usual ML cost trap — so undeploy or use batch endpoints where possible. GPU VMs are pricey; low-priority/Spot VMs cut training cost. Levers: scale clusters to zero, stop idle compute instances, avoid idle online endpoints.
gotchas: Managed online endpoints bill for their VMs continuously — idle endpoints are a common waste; use batch or undeploy.
Compute instances (dev) don't auto-stop by default — a running instance keeps billing; enable idle shutdown.
GPU compute is expensive; use low-priority/Spot VMs for interruptible training.
The v1 vs v2 SDK/CLI split caused confusion historically — use the current v2 tooling.
For generative AI, the model lives in Azure OpenAI, not Azure ML — don't conflate the two.
